summary: Astro Outpost: Moon vs Mars Survival Challenge is a browser game where kids 7–12 command a lunar or Martian base. Each Sol brings a trade-off — save power or take radiation, grow food or run science — with every choice reshaping oxygen, battery, shielding, crew health, and research output. Events are grounded in real NASA data (DONKI, OSDR, Apollo, ISS ECLSS), and two difficulty modes reflect actual planetary differences: the Moon's brutal surface versus Mars's comparative hospitality. It matters because it turns "deep space is hard" from a poster fact into something kids feel — the same trade-off logic NASA flight directors use every day, taught through play.
details:
Astro Outpost is a browser-based survival simulation where players ages 7–12 command a lunar or Martian outpost, balancing a 100 kW power grid across oxygen, radiation shielding, and science while facing daily trade-off events grounded in real NASA data (DONKI, OSDR, Apollo, ISS ECLSS). Every choice costs something — if any of the four life-support systems hits 0% the mission fails, while reaching 500 science points earns a Flight Director rating. It is built as a single HTML file using HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind, and vanilla JavaScript with Canvas 2D graphics, requiring no install, no account, and running anywhere a browser exists, which makes it easy for teachers to share and for judges to test.

The game's creativity lies in its counter-intuitive but scientifically accurate Moon = Hard, Mars = Easy framing — the Moon's lack of atmosphere, resources, and carbon makes it harsher than Mars despite being closer — alongside permanent mode-locking that mirrors real mission planning, transparent cost badges on every option, and a "Why This Science Matters" popup after each choice.

All of this is designed to close the "translation gap" in space education by turning abstract facts into lived decisions, with careful attention to cognitive load (only five tracked systems), inclusive accessibility, and classroom-friendliness.
